summary: Angle wraps unwrapped (whole turns of 360 degrees only), step_ups foot-frame pressure point held like curb_up, only changed recordings re-exported (15 of 488 recordings: 12 step_ups + 3 with wraps), Q01 assessment v2 on all 19,573 observations with L2 on the time table only. Failed observations 815 -> 156 (L5 590 -> 90, L2 189 -> 5, L1 40 -> 58). Independent verifier NOT yet run.
decisions_applied: José: blatant errors (+180/360) are fixed, nothing refit or tuned

L2 choice (made before any v2 result, in the module docstring and PROFILE_V2): time table only, failures mapped to the phase observations whose source span contains both samples of the jump; not scaled by sample spacing (at 392 ms the scaled limit is about 2,300 degrees and tests nothing)
agent_defaults_logged: Unwrap rule (gt23_fixes.unwrap_segments): np.unwrap (period 2 pi) of pelvis, thigh, shank and foot angles over each run of consecutive finite samples (a NaN gap is never bridged); the first sample of a distal segment run keeps the branch that puts its joint angle inside (-180,180]; joints re-differenced (hip = thigh-pelvis, knee = thigh-shank, ankle = foot-shank, same as C06); speeds re-derived with the C06 central difference and the published speed kept bit for bit where within 1e-9 rad/s (no speed changed anywhere); a recomputed value within 1e-9 rad of the published one keeps the published bits. check_whole_turns refuses any change that is not a whole multiple of 2 pi.

Step-up rule: task rule (recording task step_ups, 12 recordings, one per participant): foot-frame cop_anterior/vertical/lateral, left and right, all NaN with a stated reason in held_signals and a step-up limit note in task_info; force, plate pressure point (cop_lab_*), angles untouched. Evidence recorded per recording (heel marker height above plate surface on loaded samples, markers from the source); the 0.17 m C06 reference line is only a reference for the shares, not used in the rule.

Re-export scope: a recording is re-exported if any angle sample changes or it is a step_ups recording; the E01 export code is reused unchanged (E01 gt23_export.py and run_gt23_e01.py hashes unchanged) with the fixes applied to the C06 columns before export. Phase observations are re-interpolated from the corrected source; a phase sample interpolated between a wrapped and an unwrapped source sample changes by a fraction of a turn (4 samples in AB13, 4 in AB11) and is logged as interpolated_across_a_wrap with its changed source sample.

Q01 v2 input: per participant the E01 root minus the superseded recordings plus the E02 root; observation identities and row counts must equal E01 exactly (checked); flag step_up_cop_held added; read batches 2048 rows (v1 4096).

Pilot of the E02 export: AB13 dynamic_walk_1 (wrap), step_ups (hold), normal_walk_1 (clean, correctly not exported); Q01 v2 pilot AB10 + AB13 (the two participants with the largest unwrapped recordings and the one wrap sample).

labels.run_2.0_2.5: Flight is present in all checkable cycles (2.0 m/s: 347 of 347, 2.5 m/s: 359 of 359; 89 of 795 cannot be checked), so the labels stay run. The publisher README text (walking at 2.0 and 2.5 m/s) disagrees with the data: recorded here as a README error; no relabel. No walking control exists (right plate NaN in 1.2/1.8 m/s walking), so the flight statistic is not calibrated against walking.
labels.normal_walk_unlabelled: 511 of the 1,716 normal_walk_unlabelled cycles show flight (both legs under 20 N, median 21 percent of the cycle); recorded, NOT relabelled, no label invented; for the other 1,205 no plate pair is available. Source: GT23-Q01 handoff (not recomputed here).

odd_or_limits: AB10 meander_1 (right foot) and AB11 turn_and_step_1 (left foot): after the unwrap the foot angle drifts continuously to -483 and -805 degrees and the ankle to -477 and -773 degrees. The unwrap is faithful to the continuous series, but a sagittal foot angle that turns more than a full turn is not a branch-cut problem: the foot sits about 180 degrees from the shank for thousands of samples (published ankle near +-180, already failing L1). Cause unresolved (not examined: heading frame or heel/toe marker problem). Needs José: keep the continuous values, return to the published +-180 values for these two recordings, or hold the foot and ankle angles there. Not decided here; 20 more AB11 phase observations fail L1 as a consequence.
The rule asked for continuous segment angles; the same rule moves the first-sample branch only to put the joint inside (-180,180].
